proposals.minimal_demo:
Organisms, CPU or small GPU.
- Six single-type organisms plus one mixed-type organism: a 4-layer, d = 256 transformer trained on a corpus that interleaves all latent types.
- Pass criteria:
  1. Type-classification accuracy above 90% on declared latents (recovered type versus true type).
  2. Latent recovery above 0.9 (cosine or circular correlation with the exact posterior coordinates; barycentric R² for the simplex).
  3. Standard TopK, BatchTopK, Matryoshka and JumpReLU SAEs fail on non-point types in the predicted ways: tiling of circles and simplices, composite latents for bindings, and absorption in the taxonomy. These are quantified with the same metrics.
  4. The null-calibrated pipeline reports less than 5% of the trained-network structure in random-init and shuffled-latent controls.
  5. The selected L0 and width per type fall within 20% of the true generative sparsity, where SAE L0 heuristics are off.

LM census, one GPU.
- Models: GPT-2 small and Pythia-70m/160m/410m.
- Pass criteria:
  - per-layer type fractions are stable across 3 seeds (±3 percentage points) and vary smoothly with scale;
  - at equal bits per token, the typed decomposition's fitted width-scaling asymptote is significantly below the TopK SAE floor;
  - the typed atoms explain at least 50% of the linearly predictable SAE error.
- Hypothesis H_linear ('beyond noise, nearly all structure is point atoms') is supported if point atoms take more than 90% of bits saved; otherwise it is rejected in favour of a typed ontology.
proposals.compute_needs:
- Organism generation, the exact forward algorithm and training: CPU-feasible, minutes to a few hours per organism. A single GPU makes sweeps fast.
- Typed decompositions on organisms: CPU or GPU, hours.
- LM census: about 20–60 GPU-hours on one 24–80 GB GPU for GPT-2 small and Pythia up to 410m, covering about 6 layers × 3 seeds × typed and baseline dictionaries on 50–100M tokens each. Pythia-1.4b is optional.
- Reuses interp-lab for activation caching and SAE baselines.
proposals.risks:
- MDL comparisons across heterogeneous atom types depend on precision and parameter-coding choices. Mitigations: report curves against precision and budget, and calibrate the precision on the organisms.
- Organisms may not reflect LLM regimes (scale, Zipfian features, superposition load). Mitigations: Zipf-distributed feature frequencies and overcomplete latent counts in the generator.
- The project depends on proposals 1 and 2 for chart and bound atoms. It should be staged: point + dense + simplex + chart first, then bound.
- Census numbers depend on decomposition capacity and on the type menu. A type the menu omits ends up in noise, so the residual must be reported as 'unexplained' rather than 'noise'.
- Risk of being perceived as a benchmark. The core deliverable is a hypothesis test about LM ontology plus a dark-matter account, with the organisms serving as validation.

surveys.lens_summary:
STATE OF THE ART: CIRCUIT DISCOVERY AND ATTRIBUTION, 2025-2026

There are two paradigms, and both now have known failure modes.

(1) Component-level circuit discovery. This covers heads, MLPs and edges between them.
- Main methods: ACDC (https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.14997), EAP (https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10348), EAP-IG (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17806), edge pruning (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16778), position-aware EAP (https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.141.pdf) and path patching.
- The MIB benchmark (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13151) finds that attribution and mask-optimization methods do best.
- The evaluation foundations are shaky:
  - Faithfulness scores swing with ablation choices (Miller et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08734).
  - Circuits are non-identifiable (Meloux et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20914).
  - Discovery algorithms sample from an equivalence class of subgraphs rather than recovering one mechanism ("Many Circuits, One Mechanism", TMLR 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06267).
  - Activation-patching estimates are contaminated by hidden interaction effects ("Curse of Multiple Mediators", Jun 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27510).
  - Self-repair hides backup components; conditional co-ablation recovers IOI backups (CoAx, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01940).
- Interactions between components are an active 2026 topic: ProxySPEX (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17495) and the uniqueness/redundancy/synergy decomposition Stochastic Hi-Fi (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19410).
- Weights-only global maps have appeared, e.g. "Communication Map of a Transformer" (Aug 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22007), which recovers induction circuits from weight coupling alone.

(2) Feature-level attribution graphs.
- Lineage: Sparse Feature Circuits (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19647), then transcoders (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11944) and skip transcoders (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18823), then Anthropic's cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) with linearized attribution graphs (Ameisen et al. 2025, https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/methods.html; Biology, https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/biology.html).
- Extensions:
  - QK attributions for attention (Kamath et al., Jul 2025, https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attention-qk/index.html).
  - The open-source circuit-tracer library and Neuronpedia (https://aclanthology.org/2025.blackboxnlp-1.14.pdf).
  - Lorsa sparse attention (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20938) and OpenMOSS "complete replacement models".
  - Gemma Scope 2 (Dec 2025, https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/YQro5LyYjDzZrBCdb/announcing-gemma-scope-2). It ships per-layer transcoders for all Gemma 3 sizes (PT and IT) and CLTs for the 270M and 1B models, so the same small model has both transcoder kinds.
  - CLT-Forge (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21014).
  - Neuron-basis circuits that are as sparse as SAE circuits (Arora et al., ICML 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22594).
  - Sparse Weight Decomposition (Aug 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03913).
  - Sparse mixtures of linear transforms, MOLT (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/bulk-update/index.html).
  - Weight-sparse models with known circuits (Gao et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13653; weights at https://github.com/openai/circuit_sparsity).
  - Parameter-space decomposition: APD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14926) and SPD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20790), still mostly toy-scale.

WHERE CURRENT METHODS BREAK (with evidence)

(a) Mechanistic faithfulness of the replacement model.
- Olah's note (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/faithfulness-toy-model/index.html) says failure here "cuts at the very heart" of the field. It shows Jacobian matching only on toy problems (abs(x) and a memorized repeated datapoint).
- Lange et al. (Feb 2026, ICML 2026, https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/6CS2NDmoLCFcEJMor/cross-layer-transcoders-are-incentivized-to-learn-unfaithful) prove in a Boolean toy that CLTs are pushed by sparsity penalties to rewrite deep circuits as shallow ones. On Gemma-2-2B, CLT graphs pile up in layers 0-1, while per-layer transcoder graphs do not.
- SAEs can reach about 71% explained variance while recovering only about 9% of ground-truth features (Korznikov et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14111).
- No accepted edge-level faithfulness measure exists for real models.

(b) Graphs are per-prompt execution traces.
- "Can we merge attribution graphs ... global circuit picture?" is an explicit open question in the Circuits Research Landscape (Anthropic, GDM, Goodfire, EleutherAI and Decode, Aug 2025, https://www.neuronpedia.org/graph/info).
- Naive global weights suffer from interference.
- 2026 aggregation work does not learn a reusable dictionary of mechanisms: HAGD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12879), concept-targeted attribution (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27510) and circuit-signature logic (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21303).

(c) Transcoders "shatter" geometry.
- Addition becomes lookup-table features (MOLT post; Landscape). Yet real mechanisms are manifolds:
  - Counting manifolds in line-breaking (Gurnee et al., https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/linebreaks/index.html).
  - A number helix used for addition (https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00873).
  - Circular day and month features (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14860).
- 2026 manifold-aware dictionaries exist only for representations, not circuits: SASA (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06333), Bhalla and Fel (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.28119) and SMIXAE (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09224).

(d) Other gaps:
- Error nodes are "too prevalent" (Landscape).
- Suppression ("why not B") and inhibition of inactive features are missing.
- Graphs are linear: frozen attention and layer norm hide AND/OR logic.
- Long contexts are out of reach.

WHAT IS MISSING
An instrument that is trustworthy (each edge certified against the real model), global (a catalog of mechanisms with measured coverage) and uses the right units (variables and operations, not just sparse binary features).

The three proposals below each attack one of these and stack into a single tool:
- Proposal 1 is the foundation and doubles as the evaluation harness for the other two. It has the most decisive falsifiable demo.
- Proposal 2 is the highest-upside landmark result.
- Proposal 3 is the boldest change in the field's ontology.

They can interoperate with the user's interp-lab by exporting edge-level certificates into its evidence grading and its validate-attribution-graph command, without duplicating it.

CAVEAT
The shared web-search budget ran out near the end of research. Two checks remain open:
- I could not run a final check for a late-2026 paper that quantifies edge-level interventional faithfulness of attribution graphs on real models.
- I could not resolve a "Michaud 2026" quanta follow-up that a 2026 paper cites (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06888).

The implementing agent should do a quick novelty re-check on both before committing.

proposals.title: Mediation-Faithful Circuit Tracing: test every attribution-graph edge against the real model, and train replacement models that pass (mediated Jacobian matching plus interventional consistency)
proposals.gap:
WHAT IS UNSOLVED
Attribution graphs describe the replacement model, not the real one. Whether the replacement uses the same mechanisms is called the central problem by Anthropic (Olah 2025: it "cuts at the very heart"). Their only fix, Jacobian matching, was shown on one-layer toy problems.

EVIDENCE IT IS OPEN
- Lange et al. (Feb 2026; ICML 2026) prove CLT sparsity penalties reward collapsing deep circuits into shallow ones. On (a XOR b) AND (c XOR d), a CLT reconstructs perfectly with zero layer-1 features.
- On GPT-2 small and Gemma-2-2B, CLT and per-layer-transcoder (PLT) graphs tell different depth stories and give different accounts of memorization. Nobody knows which is right.
- The Aug 2025 Landscape doc says error nodes "block us from tracing" and that KL fine-tuning did not help.
- Circuit faithfulness metrics are non-robust (Miller 2024) and contaminated by interaction effects (Vaidyanathan 2026).
- SAEs can score well on reconstruction while recovering about 9% of true features (Korznikov 2026).
- No accepted, edge-level, real-model faithfulness measure exists. Anthropic's perturbation checks are qualitative case studies.
proposals.idea:
(1) THE GAUGE: an edge-level mediation test suite for any attribution graph
- Source test: for an edge u->v, write a perturbation (+-alpha, zero-ablation or resample) along u's decoder direction into the REAL model's residual stream. Run the real model forward and read v's pre-activation through v's encoder. Compare with the graph's predicted change.
- Mediator test (the one that catches CLT shortcuts): intervene on the real residual at layers between u and v, on directions the graph says are irrelevant and on directions it says mediate.
  - Perturbing other intermediate variables (the XOR nodes in Lange's toy) changes the real output but not a shortcut CLT's.
  - This separates harmless relay collapse (one direction carried along) from genuine computation collapse.
- Joint test: pairwise interventions measure "interaction mass" (the effect of both minus each alone), which every linear graph reports as zero.
- Each is run with frozen attention (local) and with live attention (global).
- Scores, per layer and per edge type with bootstrap CIs:
  - Edge Mediation Fidelity (EMF).
  - Path-Depth Fidelity.
  - Off-distribution Steering Prediction.
  - Interaction-mass fraction.

(2) THE FIX: train transcoders and CLTs with mediated Jacobian matching (MJM)
- For every layer m, add a Hutchinson estimator of ||J_MLPm(x_m) v - J_Rm(x_m) v||^2.
- J_Rm is the derivative of the replacement's layer-m output reconstruction with respect to layer m's OWN input residual. For a CLT this excludes earlier features' cross-layer decoders, so shortcuts are penalized.
- Relay-tolerant variant: project out the decoder directions of cross-layer writers. CLTs may then still collapse pure relays but not real computation.
- Add a finite-perturbation interventional-consistency term, using feature-direction perturbations drawn from the dictionary, so gates beyond first order (AND/XOR) are matched.
- Add a Jacobian-L1 term against gradient masking (a risk Olah raises).
- Low-rank or top-singular-subspace matching respects superposition: Olah argues the tail should not be matched.

(3) THE OUTPUT
Certified graphs, with a faithfulness score on every edge and node, plus a Pareto frontier of graph simplicity (nodes needed for 80% replacement score) against mediation fidelity.
proposals.why_new_understanding:
- It gives the first quantitative answer to "what fraction of what attribution graphs show is true of the network?" and turns graphs from hypotheses into tested claims.
- It settles a concrete open dispute: are LLM computations really shallow (the CLT picture, layers 0-1 heavy) or deep and multi-hop (the PLT picture)? The output is measured effective-depth profiles that can be checked against Csordas et al. 2025 (later layers contribute less, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13898).
- It measures how much computation is non-additive (interaction mass), a quantity no linear graph can report.
- It lets published case studies (multi-hop recall, planning) be re-graded edge by edge.
- Because a feature- or circuit-level claim is only as good as the replacement model under it, a validated faithful-CLT objective would change how every attribution graph is built.

proposals.minimal_demo:
STAGE 1: GROUND TRUTH (CPU, hours)
- Build a suite of known-circuit models:
  - Lange-style residual MLPs computing random Boolean DAGs of depth 2-4 with known intermediate variables, including (a XOR b) AND (c XOR d).
  - 2-4 layer transformers trained with SIIT on InterpBench circuits.
  - Optionally OpenAI csp_yolo1, whose pruned circuits are known.
- Train four replacements at matched reconstruction MSE: PLT, CLT, CLT+MJM, and CLT+MJM+interventional consistency.
- Metrics: edge precision and recall against the true DAG, recovered depth, and EMF.
- Pre-registered success:
  - Standard CLTs recover the true depth in under 30% of cases, reproducing Lange.
  - CLT+MJM recovers it in at least 90%, costing at most 10% in L0 or MSE.
  - The gauge's EMF ranks the four replacements in the same order as ground-truth edge F1 (Spearman at least 0.8). This validates the gauge itself.

STAGE 2: REAL MODELS (one GPU)
- Models:
  - Gemma 3 270M, using Gemma Scope 2's public PLTs and CLTs, so both kinds exist on the same model.
  - GPT-2 small, with public transcoders and a self-trained CLT.
- Build graphs for about 500 prompts: multi-hop recall, IOI, 2-digit addition, induction and rhyme.
- Run the gauge.
- Pre-registered predictions:
  - CLT edges have significantly lower EMF than PLT edges, concentrated in cross-layer decoder edges that span more than 2 layers.
  - Fine-tuning the Gemma Scope 2 CLT with MJM raises mean edge EMF Spearman by at least 0.2 absolute while keeping graph size within 1.5x of the original CLT.
  - Depth profiles of the faithful graphs differ from CLT profiles (KS test, p<0.01).
- Falsification: if PLT and CLT show equal EMF, or MJM cannot move EMF without destroying sparsity, the thesis fails. That negative would itself be publishable.
proposals.compute_needs:
- Stage 1: laptop CPU, minutes to hours per model.
- Stage 2 gauge: about 500 graphs, each with tens to hundreds of real-model forward passes for the sampled edges. That is roughly 0.5-1 GPU-day on a single 24 GB GPU, and about 1 week on CPU for 270M.
- MJM fine-tuning of the Gemma 3 270M CLT on about 100-200M tokens: 1-3 GPU-days on one A100 or L4-class GPU. Jacobian-vector products via torch.func add about 2-3x per-step cost.
- A GPT-2 small CLT trained from scratch needs similar compute.
- Scales in principle: Hutchinson JVPs are O(1) extra passes per layer, so MJM extends to any model where CLTs are trainable.
proposals.risks:
- Superposition means the Jacobian cannot be matched perfectly. Mitigation: match the top-singular subspace or a low-rank part only, and report sensitivity.
- Gradient masking: the replacement could fit derivatives while doing something else. Mitigation: Jacobian-L1 plus finite-perturbation consistency.
- Decoder-direction interventions push real activations off-distribution. Mitigation: report resample and mean-ablation variants and dose-response curves.
- "Faithful" is ambiguous for CLT relay collapse. Mitigation: treat it as a dial and a Pareto frontier, not a binary.
- MJM may simply turn CLTs back into PLTs and lose their compactness. That is still a clear answer, and the relay-tolerant variant tests whether a middle ground exists.
- Live-attention tests are costly and noisy.
- Overlap risk with an unseen late-2026 paper: the search budget ran out before a final check, so re-check novelty before building.

proposals.title: Mechanism Dictionary Learning ("CircuitAtlas"): sparse coding over per-token attribution graphs to get a global, causally validated catalog of a model's mechanisms, and the first mechanism-level census and scaling law
proposals.gap:
WHAT IS UNSOLVED
Attribution graphs are per-prompt execution traces. "Can we merge attribution graphs, or otherwise obtain a more global circuit picture?" is an explicit open problem in the multi-lab Circuits Research Landscape (Aug 2025). Ameisen et al. list global circuits as a limitation; their global weights suffer interference, and TWERA virtual weights average over prompts rather than decompose them.

WHY EXISTING GLOBAL APPROACHES FALL SHORT
- Quanta discovery (Michaud 2023) and Sparse Feature Circuits (Marks 2024) cluster TOKENS by gradients or activations. That assigns one behavior per token and cannot represent several mechanisms co-occurring.
- APD and SPD decompose PARAMETERS but have only been shown on toy models and a GPT-2-small pilot.
- 2026 aggregation work works inside one graph or compares hand-picked circuits; none learns a reusable dictionary of mechanisms with measured coverage of the model's loss:
  - HAGD does spectral coarsening within a graph.
  - Concept-targeted attribution builds graphs toward probe directions.
  - The causal-functional-signature work compares given circuits with logic programs.
  - Circuit-Diff's supernode aggregation was released unevaluated.
- "Many Circuits, One Mechanism" (2026) shows single-prompt circuits are samples from an equivalence class, another reason to aggregate.

The result: nobody can say how many mechanisms a model has, what fraction of its loss a given set of circuits explains, or whether larger models add mechanisms or refine them.
proposals.idea:
KEY INSIGHT
Transcoder features give every token's graph a SHARED coordinate system, so graphs from different inputs can be compared without graph matching.

1. EMBED
For each token position t in a corpus, compute the influence of every edge on that token's loss (or correct-logit margin). Each edge is keyed by:
- source feature;
- target feature, or logit;
- relation: same position, or carried through attention (optionally which head, following Kamath et al.).
Positions are collapsed. This gives a sparse vector e_t over a fixed edge vocabulary.

Efficiency: build one full sequence graph per context and extract every position's influence subgraph with sparse linear algebra, (I-A)^-1 restricted to each target. This avoids one circuit-tracer run per token.

2. DECOMPOSE
Learn an overcomplete, non-negative sparse dictionary e_t ~ sum_k c_tk M_k:
- A graph SAE with a TopK encoder over sparse inputs and non-negative sparse decoder atoms.
- An NMF / online-LDA baseline, where tokens are documents and edges are words.
- A path-coherence prior so atoms form connected input-to-output subgraphs.
- A linearized causal term: removing an atom should reduce the target in proportion to its coefficient.
Each atom M_k is a candidate mechanism. A token's computation is a sparse combination of mechanisms, so overlapping and composing mechanisms are allowed, unlike clustering.

3. VALIDATE IN THE REAL MODEL
- Ablate each atom with feature-level path patching along its edges, on tokens where it is active.
- Measure predicted versus actual change in loss.
- Measure specificity: the effect on tokens where the atom is inactive should be near zero.
- Auto-label atoms from their top tokens and subgraphs.

4. SCIENCE
- Coverage curve: fraction of loss attribution explained as a function of the number of atoms K.
- Mechanism frequency distribution and its exponent.
- "Monogenic" tokens (one mechanism) versus "polygenic" tokens (many).
- Cross-model matching. Gemma 3 270M and 1B share a tokenizer and both have Gemma Scope 2 transcoders, so features can be aligned by activation correlation.
- Mechanism-level diff of PT versus IT models; Gemma Scope 2 ships transcoders for both.
proposals.why_new_understanding:
- It moves circuit work from anecdotes ("here is the circuit for this prompt") to a census: "on corpus D, X% of this model's next-token loss is accounted for by K causally verified mechanisms, with frequencies following law F."
- It is the first direct, mechanistic test of the quantization model of neural scaling. Michaud et al. predict a power law in the frequency of discrete skills tied to the loss-scaling exponent. Here the skills are causally validated subgraphs rather than gradient clusters. The test is falsifiable both ways.
- It answers whether larger models add new mechanisms or refine shared ones (universality at the mechanism level), and what instruction tuning changes mechanistically.
- It is the analogue of the SAE step-change, applied to computation instead of representation.

proposals.minimal_demo:
CPU TIER
- Model: GPT-2 small with public Dunefsky transcoders, or TinyStories-33M with self-trained PLTs.
- Data: about 20k token positions, keeping the top 500 influence edges per position.

GPU TIER
- Model: Gemma 3 270M with Gemma Scope 2 16k "small-L0" PLTs.
- Data: 100k positions of mixed web, code and math text, then a repeat on Gemma 3 1B and on the IT checkpoints.

BASELINES
- QDG gradient clustering.
- k-means on edge vectors.
- NMF on feature co-occurrence (to rule out the "atoms are just co-active features" explanation).
- Random edge partitions.

PRE-REGISTERED SUCCESS CRITERIA
1. Coverage: K of at most 2k atoms reconstruct at least 70% of held-out edge-influence mass with at most 10 active atoms per token.
2. Causal validity: on held-out tokens, Spearman of at least 0.6 between predicted and real-model loss change under atom ablation, and a specificity ratio (effect on active versus inactive tokens) of at least 5x.
3. Atoms beat QDG and clustering baselines on causal validity at equal K, and beat co-occurrence NMF on specificity.
4. Blinded LLM-judge and spot human ratings prefer atom descriptions over QDG clusters.
5. Science readouts with confidence intervals:
   - power-law fit and exponent of atom frequencies, compared with the exponent the quantization model implies from Gemma 3 or Pythia loss scaling;
   - fraction of 270M atoms matched in 1B;
   - the list of atoms gained or lost from PT to IT.

FALSIFICATION
If atoms fail the specificity test, or merely reproduce feature co-occurrence, the method fails. If frequencies are not heavy-tailed, the quantization model fails at the mechanism level.

- Graph extraction dominates.
- CPU tier: about 20k positions for GPT-2 small overnight on a multi-core CPU.
- GPU tier: about 100k positions, at roughly 0.5-2 s per sequence graph with pruning and amortizing all positions of a sequence, is about 1-3 GPU-days for 270M on a single 24-48 GB GPU, and about 2x that for 1B.

proposals.risks:
- Atoms may only mirror feature co-occurrence. Mitigation: the co-occurrence NMF baseline, plus the path-coherence and causal terms.
- Error nodes may carry a large share of influence. Mitigation: report the error share, and use Proposal 1's faithful transcoders.
- Attention-mediated edges depend on position and on QK. Mitigation: relation types first, head and QK annotation later.
- Validating with the same linearization would be circular. Mitigation: real-model ablations are the primary metric.
- Mechanisms may be continuous or manifold-like rather than discrete. That would itself be a finding, and it links to Proposal 3.
- Graph extraction cost at scale.
- Gemma Scope 2 transcoders may change with sparsity level. Mitigation: check that the census is stable across the small, medium and big L0 variants.

proposals.title: From features to variables and operators: geometry-preserving circuit tracing with subspace nodes and matrix-valued, typed operator edges that automatically recover algorithms (clocks, counters, rotations)
proposals.gap:
WHAT IS UNSOLVED
Transcoder attribution graphs "shatter" geometry.
- Anthropic found that addition decomposes into lookup-table features such as "6+9=5 (mod 10)". They call this inefficient and say it misses key structure (MOLT update; Landscape 2025).
- Olah lists "simplicity" (feature manifolds approximated by many discrete features) as the second major concern after faithfulness.

EVIDENCE IT IS OPEN
- The most striking real mechanisms were all found largely by hand:
  - counting manifolds that attention heads "twist" (Gurnee et al., Oct 2025);
  - the number helix and the "Clock" algorithm for addition (Kantamneni and Tegmark 2025);
  - circular day and month features (Engels et al. 2024);
  - the Fourier clock algorithm in grokked modular addition (Nanda et al. 2023).
- 2026 manifold-aware dictionaries (SASA, SMIXAE, Bhalla and Fel) model REPRESENTATIONS only.
- MOLT and MxD model OPERATIONS, but their nodes remain 1-D features.
- No tool outputs a circuit whose nodes are continuous variables and whose edges are typed operations, so algorithms cannot be read out automatically.
proposals.idea:
1. VARIABLE DICTIONARY
Group-sparse subspace transcoders and SAEs. Each node v is a gated k_v-dimensional subspace (k from 1 to 8, rank chosen by a nuclear-norm or group-lasso penalty) with coordinates z_v(x). The dictionary is trained with Proposal 1's mediated-Jacobian loss so the variables are mechanistically faithful.

2. OPERATOR EDGES
- The edge v->w at token t is the Jacobian BLOCK J_wv(t) = dz_w/dz_v, a k_w x k_v matrix, under the frozen-attention and layer-norm linearization.
- Attention-mediated edges add the bilinear QK form, following Kamath et al.

3. OPERATOR TYPING AND GLOBALIZATION ACROSS TOKENS
Fit each edge's family of Jacobians to a small operator library:
- constant linear map (a global operation);
- rotation (orthogonal part from polar decomposition, with an angle);
- translation or shift;
- projection or threshold;
- bilinear modulation, J_wv(t) ~ sum_m z_u(t)_m B_m, meaning one variable rotates or gates another. "a+b by rotating the a-helix by an angle set by b" is then detected automatically as a bilinear operator edge.
- A residual "lookup" type for anything that does not fit.

4. OUTPUTS
- An algorithm graph of typed variables and operators.
- Quantitative counterfactual predictions, e.g. rotating input variable v by theta should rotate output w by R(theta) and change the answer to a predicted token.
- A corpus-wide census of operator types.
proposals.why_new_understanding:
- It changes the language of circuits from "which discrete features fire" to "which variables are computed and which operations act on them", i.e. from lookups to algorithms.
- It makes it possible to measure, for the first time, a basic unknown: what fraction of an LLM's computation is geometric or operator-like (rotations, shifts, comparisons on manifolds) versus memorized lookup.
- It tests whether the hand-found manifold mechanisms are rare showcases or the general case.
- If it works, mechanisms that took a paper's worth of manual effort could be recovered automatically.

proposals.minimal_demo:
(a) GROUND TRUTH: 1-layer modular-addition transformer (p=113, grokked), CPU minutes
- Success: automatically recover the 4-6 key Fourier frequencies as 2-D variables (cosine at least 0.9 to the known directions) and rotation and bilinear operator edges.
- The graph should reach at least 90% replacement score with at most 20 nodes, versus at least 200 lookup-style features for a standard transcoder at the same score.

(b) SYNTHETIC: small transformer trained on text with embedded cyclic and counting tasks (weekday or month offsets, distance to a line boundary)
- Success: recover circle and counter variables with shift and "twist" operators.
- Rotation interventions predict the model's changed answer in at least 80% of trials.

(c) REAL MODEL: Qwen2.5-0.5B, Gemma 3 1B or Llama-3.2-1B on 2-digit addition and weekday/month offset prompts
- GPT-2 cannot do the offset tasks (Engels et al.), so pick a model that solves them.
- Pre-registered metrics:
  - Description length: nodes needed for 80% task replacement score versus Gemma Scope 2 / circuit-tracer transcoder graphs; target at least 5x smaller.
  - Continuous counterfactuals: rotating the operand variable by the angle for +k changes the model's answer to a+k in at least 60% of cases, versus at most 20% for steering the best discrete transcoder features.
  - An operator census: fraction of edge mass that is constant, rotation, bilinear or lookup, with confidence intervals.

FALSIFICATION: if the subspace graphs are no smaller than the transcoder graphs, or rotation counterfactuals fail, the variables-and-operators thesis is refuted for these models.
proposals.compute_needs:
- (a) and (b): CPU or a small GPU, minutes to hours.
- (c): training subspace transcoders on 5-10 layers of a 0.5-1B model with about 50-200M tokens is 1-3 GPU-days on a single 24-80 GB GPU.
- Jacobian blocks are cheap: k_w x k_v with k at most 8.
- Operator fitting runs on CPU.
- Scales in principle like transcoders: group-sparse gating adds little cost, and edges are small dense matrices.
proposals.risks:
- Subspace dictionaries may still fragment manifolds (the "dilution" regime in Bhalla and Fel). Mitigation: rank selection plus a merge step that groups co-varying atoms.
- Gating discontinuities make Jacobian blocks noisy. Mitigation: average over neighbourhoods and use finite-difference checks.
- Small real models may implement arithmetic mostly by lookup; Kantamneni and Tegmark used models of 6B parameters and up. Mitigation: the ground-truth and synthetic tiers carry the method claim, and the real-model census reports whatever it finds. A finding that "small models are lookup-dominated" would still be informative.
- Coordinates inside a subspace are only defined up to rotation. Mitigation: canonicalize, e.g. by aligning to logit-lens or task-variable regressions.
- The operator library may miss nonlinear operations; these fall into the residual "lookup" type, which is reported.
- The demo needs Proposal 1's faithfulness objective to avoid recreating shortcut artifacts in the new basis.

surveys.lens_summary:
META-VIEW AS OF 2026-10-15 (open-problem agendas, tooling, and the user's interp-lab)

1) Agenda documents.
- Sharkey et al., 'Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability' (arXiv 2501.16496, TMLR 2025; https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16496). Its main methodological open problems are:
  - reconstruction error, or the 'dark matter' of sparse dictionary learning (SDL);
  - no agreed definition of a 'feature';
  - SDL ignores feature geometry and handles attention poorly;
  - 'describing the mechanisms directly remains unresolved';
  - validation: 'conflating hypotheses with conclusions has regrettably been commonplace', there is no consensus on model organisms, and benchmarks need ground truth (compiled programs or IIT). It also suggests MDL-style objectives in place of sparsity.
- Multi-org 'Circuits Research Landscape' (Aug 2025; https://www.neuronpedia.org/graph/info). It asks for:
  - global circuits beyond per-prompt graphs;
  - fixes for error nodes, which are 'simply too prevalent';
  - attention/QK support;
  - suppressive edges;
  - 'downstream tasks for measuring understanding'.
- GDM 'A Pragmatic Vision for Interpretability' (Dec 2025; https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/StENzDcD3kpfGJssR/a-pragmatic-vision-for-interpretability). It moves away from ambitious reverse-engineering after 'Negative Results for SAEs on Downstream Tasks' (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/4uXCAJNuPKtKBsi28/negative-results-for-saes-on-downstream-tasks).

2) Instruments that shipped in 2025-26.
- Attribution graphs over cross-layer transcoders (CLTs): https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/methods.html and biology.html.
- Open-source circuit-tracer (https://github.com/safety-research/circuit-tracer; 2.9k stars, pushed 2026-10-14). It now supports Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen3 0.6-14B per-layer transcoders (PLTs), Gemma-3 270M-27B via GemmaScope-2, and a GPT-OSS-20B CLT.
- QK attention tracing (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attention-qk/index.html); Neuronpedia reported open-model support in Apr 2026.
- Sparse mixtures of linear transforms (MOLTs; https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/bulk-update/index.html). Open questions there: how transforms enter attribution graphs, and compositional chains.
- Parameter decomposition, in three steps:
  - APD (arXiv 2501.14926);
  - SPD (arXiv 2506.20790);
  - VPD: Goodfire 'Interpreting Language Model Parameters', May 2026, a 4-layer 67M-parameter LM (https://www.goodfire.com/research/interpreting-lm-parameters). The code is https://github.com/goodfire-ai/param-decomp, whose reference config needs 32 GPUs.
- Weight-sparse transformers (arXiv 2511.13653; weights at https://github.com/openai/circuit_sparsity).
- Natural-language readouts:
  - Activation Oracles (arXiv 2512.15674).
  - Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs; https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/nla/). They reach 0.6-0.8 fraction of variance explained, but confabulate, have 'no mechanistic grounding', and are costly.
  - Flow-NLA (arXiv 2609.33702).
  - Jacobian lens / 'global workspace' (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html).
- Interference weights (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/interference_effectiveness_helpfulness/index.html). Helpful virtual weights still outnumber the original parameters, and whether a 'better basis' exists is open.
- Geometry:
  - linebreak-counting manifolds (arXiv 2601.04480);
  - Goodfire's geometric calculator in Llama-3.1-8B: 'developing methods to find such mechanisms at scale';
  - block-sparse featurizers (BSF), vision only (https://github.com/goodfire-ai/block-sparse-featurizer);
  - 'Do SAEs Capture Concept Manifolds?' (arXiv 2604.28119): SAEs 'dilute' manifolds;
  - 'When Models Don't Manipulate Manifolds' (arXiv 2609.37680).

3) The validity crisis. This is the clearest sign of what is still open.
- Paulo & Belrose (arXiv 2501.18838) replaced a Pythia-160M layer-6 transcoder's latents with activations simulated by an LLM from auto-interp explanations. The rewritten model's loss was statistically similar to zero-ablating the MLP. In other words, current explanations account for roughly zero nats of what the layer does.
- Korznikov et al. (arXiv 2602.14111): SAEs recover 9% of ground-truth features at 71% variance explained, and match random baselines on interpretability, probing and editing (0.90 vs 0.87; 0.72 vs 0.69; 0.72 vs 0.73).
- CLTs are pushed toward unfaithful shortcut circuits (https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/6CS2NDmoLCFcEJMor; ICML 2026).
- LLM simulators can bypass the explanations they are scoring (arXiv 2609.08585).
- Today, Cammarata's 'Neural Networks Are Already Clean' (https://already-clean.goodfire.com/) argues that polysemanticity is mostly not superposition. This is a live controversy, and no one has a test for it measured in nats.
- Ground truth exists only in toy form: Tracr (arXiv 2301.05062), InterpBench (arXiv 2407.14494; 86 tiny models trained with strict interchange intervention training, SIIT), and SynthSAEBench (arXiv 2602.14687).

4) Tooling.
- Existing: TransformerLens, nnsight/NDIF, nnterp, SAELens, EleutherAI sparsify and Delphi, Neuronpedia (open source since Mar 2025), circuit-tracer, CLT-Forge (arXiv 2603.21014), interp-engine (Aug 2026), and a community MOLT replication (https://github.com/Ky-Ng/repro-molts).
- Missing:
  - nothing tells you HOW MUCH of a model is understood;
  - nothing traces computation whose nodes are manifolds rather than 1-D features;
  - there is no realistic LM with a certified answer key.

5) The user's interp-lab (v3.1).
- What it does: criterion-driven feature ranking, intervention-graded evidence tiers, `calibrate` against planted synthetic worlds, cross-model fingerprints, quant-diff, and an MCP agent loop.
- Its own docs say: 'synthetic worlds certify the grading machinery, not the toolkit's behavior on messy real activations.'
- It does not measure global understanding, trace geometric circuits, or supply certified real-model ground truth. The proposals below plug into its FeatureProvider, Verbalizer and InterventionRunner adapters and into `calibrate`; they do not duplicate it.

TRACTABILITY JUDGMENT
Out of reach for a small team: frontier-scale CLTs, RL-trained NLAs on large models, and VPD.

High-leverage and within reach with one GPU plus an autonomous agent:
- (a) A metric for understanding measured in nats. This is mostly software plus LLM tokens, on Pythia, GPT-2 and Gemma-3-270M.
- (b) Circuit tracing over multi-dimensional (manifold) features. This needs single-GPU featurizer training.
- (c) Small language models with planted, certified mechanisms. This needs 30M-parameter training runs.

The three compose:
- (c) certifies (a) and (b);
- (a) scores the graphs from (b) and anyone else's explanations;
- all three resolve the superposition-versus-'already clean' question with numbers.

proposals.title: Nats of Understanding: turn explanations into executable code, swap them into the model, and measure in nats how much of a network we actually understand
proposals.gap:
The field has no measure of how much of a model's computation its explanations account for.

Evidence that this is open:
- Paulo & Belrose (arXiv 2501.18838, Pythia-160M layer 6, 32k TopK-32 transcoder): replacing every latent with LLM-simulated activations from auto-interp explanations gave loss statistically similar to zero-ablating the MLP. Explanations with good per-latent detection scores carried essentially no causal information.
- Korznikov et al. 2026 (arXiv 2602.14111): trained SAEs score about the same as random baselines on standard interpretability metrics (0.90 vs 0.87). The proxy metrics cannot tell real understanding from noise.
- Poché et al. 2026 (arXiv 2609.08585): LLM simulators can solve the task without using the explanation, so simulator-based scores are contaminated.
- NLAs (transformer-circuits.pub/2026/nla) optimize a neural reconstructor. Their 'explanations' are judged by a model, not checked as claims, and confabulate (arXiv 2609.33702).
- Sharkey et al. call for MDL-style objectives and better validation. The Circuits Landscape asks for 'downstream tasks for measuring understanding'.

No paper or tool we could find reports the fraction of a real LM's loss recovered when its units are replaced by human-readable explanations, as a function of how long those explanations are. Searches for executable/programmatic explanations with whole-model loss recovered found nothing beyond N2G-style n-gram explanations scored per neuron.
proposals.idea:
Build the 'compiler test' for interpretability, and make understanding something an agent can optimize.

(1) Explanations as programs.
- Each unit gets an explanation written in a small, readable Python DSL. Units can be MLP neurons, SAE or transcoder latents, VPD components, or weight-sparse-model neurons.
- The program predicts the unit's activation at every token.
- Primitives are vectorized and fast: token and lexicon membership, regex over decoded text, previous-k-token predicates, position and line position, bracket and quote depth, distance-since-token counters, and small piecewise-constant magnitude maps.
- Programs may also read OTHER already-explained units. This makes explanations compositional, so a fully explained model is an input-independent circuit description written as code.
- There is deliberately no 'call an LLM' primitive, which removes the simulator-shortcut problem.

(2) MDL accounting.
- Explanation cost in bits = compressed canonical AST + lexicon entries x log2(vocab) + fitted constants x 16 bits.
- Lookup tables are allowed but priced, so cheating shows up on the curve.

(3) Replacement harness.
- Swap ALL units of a layer (or the whole model) for their programs. Unexplained units are held at their mean, which is the null hypothesis.
- Run the real model on top and report CE and KL on held-out text.
- Understood Fraction UF = (CE_null - CE_expl)/(CE_null - CE_orig). Also report UF relative to the dictionary's own reconstruction ceiling.
- The output is a frontier curve UF(bits) and its area.

(4) Loss-weighted error and an agent loop.
- Attribute each explanation's error to the loss with a first-order term g_i*(a_i - a_hat_i), checked by exact swap tests.
- Give a coding agent, at each iteration, the counterexamples whose errors cost the most nats.
- Accept a program only if it improves held-out nats per bit.
- This turns 'interpret the model' into an optimization problem with a ground-truth objective, much as SAEs made 'find features' one.

(5) Baselines that anchor the frontier:
- mean/zero ablation;
- unigram and bigram token-to-activation tables;
- N2G n-gram graphs;
- a replication of Paulo & Belrose (natural-language explanation plus LLM simulator, with quantile normalization);
- the same natural-language explanation compiled once into code, with no iteration.

(6) Basis and scaling studies.
- The same harness compares bases at equal bits: dense neurons, transcoder latents, SAE latents, OpenAI weight-sparse neurons, and released VPD components where available.
- It also runs across Pythia sizes and checkpoints.

Integration with interp-lab: it exports feature cards and explanations into the harness, and the harness returns a new 'replacement-verified (nats)' evidence tier to interp-lab's grader.
proposals.why_new_understanding:
It would give the first number-with-error-bars answer to 'how much of GPT-2 or Pythia do we understand?', stated as nats recovered per kilobyte of human-readable code, layer by layer.

Questions it would answer:
- (a) Superposition versus Cammarata's 'already clean' claim, decided in the model's own currency. If neuron-basis code reaches the same UF per bit as transcoder-basis code, decomposition is unnecessary. If transcoder-basis code wins by a lot, superposition is doing real work.
- (b) How explainability scales with model size, depth and training step. This would be a first interpretability scaling law, using Pythia's 70m-1.4b models and their checkpoints trained on identical data.
- (c) Where the 'dark nats' live: which contexts and token types resist short explanations. This is a map of the frontier of our ignorance.
- (d) Whether weight-sparse training (arXiv 2511.13653) buys explainability per nat, and how much: a quantitative test of its '16x smaller circuits' claim.

Because explanations can reference other explanations, the end state is a decompiled model: a global circuit description that runs. That addresses the global-circuits and validation problems at the same time. Either outcome is a landmark. A positive result shows unit-level understanding can be made causally complete. A negative result, under a generous bit and agent budget, would be strong evidence that mid-layer computation is not describable at unit level, which would redirect the field.

proposals.minimal_demo:
Stage A (CPU-feasible, about 1 week of agent time):
- Harness, DSL, bit accounting and baselines on Pythia-70m (6 layers, 2048 MLP neurons per layer) and GPT-2 small layers 0-2.
- Rank units by loss relevance and explain them in that order.
- Success: (i) a sanity calibration showing unigram/bigram tables recover a large share of layer-0 MLP function; (ii) agent-refined code beats N2G and NL+simulator by at least 3x in UF at equal bits on layers 1-3.

Stage B (1 GPU), the headline experiment, which replicates Paulo & Belrose exactly:
- Train a Pythia-160M layer-6 TopK transcoder (32k latents, k=32) with EleutherAI sparsify.
- Run the NL+simulator baseline from that paper.
- Run loss-guided code explanations under a fixed budget, for example 50M agent tokens.
- Pre-registered success: code explanations recover at least 40% of the transcoder's own CE recovery relative to zero ablation, versus about 0% for the baseline, with bootstrap CIs over held-out Pile tokens.
- Pre-registered falsification: below 10% at the full budget. That is published as a negative result.

Stage C, basis adjudication:
- Compute UF(bits) frontiers at early, middle and late layers of Pythia-70m/160m for dense neurons and transcoder latents.
- Add one OpenAI weight-sparse model from openai/circuit_sparsity.
- Report which basis dominates at equal bits; this is the 'already clean' test.

Stage D, scaling:
- Compare bits needed for UF = 0.5 at matched relative depth across Pythia 70m/160m/410m.
- Track it across 5 training checkpoints of one model.

Deliverables:
- a pip-installable harness;
- versioned explanation programs;
- frontier plots;
- an interp-lab evidence exporter.
proposals.compute_needs:
Model side:
- Pythia-70m/160m forward passes over about 1-5M held-out tokens are fine on CPU (minutes to an hour) and take seconds on a GPU.
- Activation caches are a few GB.
- Training the Pythia-160M transcoder takes about 2-6 GPU-hours on one 24GB GPU, for 0.3-1B tokens.

Agent side:
- About 30-80M LLM tokens to write and refine programs for about 2-5k high-relevance units.
- Fallback: a local 7-14B coder model on the same GPU.

Program execution is vectorized numpy over precomputed token-feature tables, so it is negligible.

Total: about 1 GPU-week plus the LLM-token budget. Pythia 410m in Stage D roughly doubles this.
proposals.risks:
- Deep-layer units may be inexpressible in surface primitives. Mitigations are compositional references and allowing explanations over earlier explained units. If it still fails, that failure is the scientific finding.
- Errors from thousands of small units could compound. Mitigations are reporting the curve as more units are explained, and fitting magnitudes explicitly.
- Goodharting on evaluation text. Mitigations are strict train/held-out splits, an MDL acceptance rule, and periodic fresh-corpus evaluation.
- The choice of bit accounting is somewhat arbitrary. Mitigations are reporting several codings and checking that frontier orderings are robust.
- LLM cost overruns. Mitigation: prioritize units by loss relevance, which concentrates most nats in a minority of units.
- Interpretability may still be disputed: code could be 'correct but unreadable'. Mitigations are a cap on per-program size and a human readability audit of sampled programs.

proposals.title: Geometric Circuit Tracing: attribution graphs whose nodes are manifolds and whose edges are named geometric operations
proposals.gap:
Every open circuit tool (circuit-tracer, CLT-Forge, Neuronpedia graphs) uses 1-D features as nodes. Recent work shows this breaks continuous representations into pieces.

Evidence that this is open:
- 'Do SAEs Capture Concept Manifolds?' (arXiv 2604.28119) finds SAEs 'dilute' manifolds.
- Michaud et al. (arXiv 2509.02565) analyse SAE scaling in the presence of feature manifolds.
- Anthropic's MOLT note says transcoders 'shatter' computation, for example implementing addition as many lookup-table features.
- The best geometric mechanisms were all found by hand: Anthropic's linebreak counting manifolds that attention heads 'twist' (arXiv 2601.04480); Goodfire's 'geometric calculator', mod-2/5/10 circles in Llama-3.1-8B, whose authors say they are 'developing methods to find such mechanisms at scale' and that causal evidence used steering at many times natural norm; and Kantamneni & Tegmark's helix addition.
- MOLTs leave open how transforms enter attribution graphs and whether chained transforms compose.
- Block-sparse featurizers exist for vision (Goodfire BSF, July 2026), with community LM ports, but they are representational only. They do not trace computation between blocks.
- We found no method that builds end-to-end graphs whose nodes are multi-dimensional manifolds and whose edges are characterized as operations such as rotation, translation, projection or alignment.
proposals.idea:
Build a replacement model and attribution pipeline in which the unit of analysis is a low-dimensional block.

(1) Block featurizers on residual streams.
- Use BSF-style block-TopK with k = 2-8 dimensions per block.
- Each block carries a presence (its norm) and a coordinate (where on the manifold the activation sits).

(2) Block transcoders replacing MLPs.
- These are sparse, gated, low-rank maps in the MOLT style, re-expressed block to block: E_ij = D_j^+ (U_t V_t) D_i, a k_out x k_in matrix.
- Attention is handled with frozen patterns, as in circuit-tracer, plus a QK bilinear form between query and key blocks for attention-mediated alignment.

(3) Geometric attribution.
- Linearize with frozen gates, LayerNorm and attention, as in Ameisen et al.
- Compute block-to-block Jacobian edges across layers and positions, and prune by contribution norm.

(4) Automatic operation labelling for each strong edge.
- Run a polar/SVD decomposition, then fit operation templates: rotation by theta (for example 'add k on a cycle'), scaling, rank-reducing projection (a read-out or comparison), translation via gated bias, and QK 'offset alignment' (attend to the item at manifold offset delta, the linebreak 'twist').
- Express each edge in fitted manifold coordinates (circle phase, helix, line) found with Fourier and persistent-homology fits.

(5) Verification by natural-norm geometric interventions.
- Move a block's coordinate along its fitted manifold while keeping its norm, and check that the downstream output shifts as the edge labels predict.

Output: circuit-tracer-compatible JSON, so graphs render in Neuronpedia-style viewers, plus an operations catalog per model.
proposals.why_new_understanding:
It lets the field see continuous-variable computation automatically, as compact algorithms instead of hundreds of lookup features. Examples are counting, calendar and number arithmetic, comparison, position and length tracking, and spatial and temporal reasoning.

It makes the open empirical question measurable: what fraction of an LM's computation is geometric (rotations and alignments on low-dimensional manifolds) versus lookup or linear readout? 'When Models Don't Manipulate Manifolds' (arXiv 2609.37680) shows the answer is not always 'geometric'.

Compressing a graph from about 100 nodes to about 10 would make circuit analysis of these behaviours tractable for humans and agents. The operations catalog would show which geometric primitives recur across tasks and models; Goodfire's calculator suggests reuse. That moves from case studies toward general laws.

Combined with Proposal 1, a geometric graph is itself a short program whose nats can be scored.

proposals.minimal_demo:
(1) Ground-truth sanity check:
- Grokked modular-addition transformer (Nanda et al., arXiv 2301.05217), plus a small transformer trained on synthetic day/month/hour arithmetic with distractor features in superposition.
- Success: (i) recover the key Fourier frequencies as 2-D blocks; (ii) label the relevant edges as rotations with angle error under 5 degrees; (iii) operation-classification accuracy above 90%; (iv) a graph of 10 or fewer nodes explains at least 90% of logit difference, where SAE/PLT graphs need at least 10x more nodes.

(2) Real models:
- GPT-2 small greater-than (Hanna et al., arXiv 2305.00586).
- Day/month '+k' arithmetic and counting/line-length tasks in Gemma-2-2B, Qwen3-0.6B, Pythia-1.4B and Gemma-3-270M. Public PLTs are available as baselines via circuit-tracer.
- Pre-registered metrics:
  - (a) nodes needed for 80% graph faithfulness, block graph versus circuit-tracer PLT/CLT graph; predicted compression of at least 5x;
  - (b) natural-norm geometric interventions predict the answer shift (for example, rotating the day-block phase by 2 x 2pi/7 gives day+2), with top-1 agreement of 70% or more versus a linear-steering baseline;
  - (c) block-transcoder fraction of variance unexplained (FVU) at matched L0 and parameter count versus PLTs, testing the MOLT claim on open models.
- Falsification: compression under 1.5x on tasks with known circular representations. That would mean the geometry is representational while the computation is effectively lookup or linear, which is itself an important finding.
proposals.compute_needs:
- Toy models: CPU, minutes to hours.
- Block featurizers and transcoders: about 100-300M activation tokens per layer, roughly 1-3 GPU-hours per layer for GPT-2 small or Pythia on a 24GB GPU, and about 2-3x that for Gemma-2-2B (d=2304). A focused demo covering 4-6 layers x 3 models fits in about 2-4 GPU-days.
- Attribution: per-prompt Jacobians over k x k blocks are cheaper than over 1-D features at equal coverage.
- No LLM-agent budget is required, though an agent can label operations.
proposals.risks:
- Scooping. Goodfire (BSF, manifold steering, a stated 'at scale' effort) and Anthropic (MOLT) are closest. Mitigations: ship open source quickly, and differentiate on the edge operations, QK alignment and verification metrics.
- Block training is unstable or splits a manifold across blocks; the community 'tournament top-k' work documents splitting. Mitigation: merge co-firing blocks.
- Basis ambiguity within a block, which canonical within-block PCA and Fourier fitting address.
- Many real computations may be gated lookup rather than smooth geometry. The method then reports that honestly, but the headline compression may be smaller than hoped.
- Small models may not perform calendar arithmetic reliably. Mitigations: use tasks they do perform (greater-than, counting, position) and use Gemma-2-2B or Qwen3 if a GPU is available.

proposals.title: Answer-Key Language Models: training realistic small LMs with certified planted mechanisms and a superposition dial, to measure when each interpretability method sees the truth
proposals.gap:
Sharkey et al. name validation as a central open problem: 'Conflating hypotheses with conclusions has regrettably been commonplace', there is no consensus on model organisms, and benchmarks need ground-truth explanations.

Ground truth today is toy-only:
- Tracr compiles tiny programs.
- InterpBench has 86 SIIT models that, by its own account, are 'very small and have very little functionality', and it evaluates only circuit-discovery algorithms.
- SynthSAEBench uses synthetic activations, not models.
- The CLT-unfaithfulness claim rests on a 4-input XOR toy plus indirect real-model evidence.
- 'Can Graph Learning Learn Circuits?' (arXiv 2608.08536) states there is no established way to obtain provably correct ground-truth circuits for real transformers.

Meanwhile the major methods (SAEs, PLTs vs CLTs, VPD, BSF, NLAs, J-lens, raw neurons) give conflicting accounts. Korznikov et al. find 9% ground-truth recovery. The superposition-versus-'already clean' debate cannot be settled without a model whose true representations are known and whose superposition density can be set on purpose.

interp-lab's own `calibrate` docs say synthetic worlds certify only the grading machinery, not behaviour on real activations.
proposals.idea:
Contract training: a recipe for training a realistic small LM that ALSO implements K planted mechanisms (K of about 50-500) with a certified internal specification.

(1) Data.
- TinyStories or FineWeb-Edu mixed with synthetic text whose latent variables are known.
- Synthetic families: multi-hop facts from a synthetic knowledge base, cyclic arithmetic (circle manifolds), counting (1-D manifolds), variable binding resolved through attention, boolean compositions such as (a XOR b) AND (c XOR d) embedded in text, and suppression/negation rules.

(2) Representation contracts.
- Variable V is encoded linearly, or on a specified circle or helix, in subspace S_V at layer l.
- This is enforced with interchange intervention training (IIT, Geiger et al.).
- The overlaps among the S_V are chosen to set a superposition dial: planted features per dimension of the contract region, from 0.25 to 16.

(3) Circuit contracts.
- V3 = f(V1, V2) is computed between specified layers through specified heads or MLP blocks.
- This is enforced with SIIT-style losses: non-circuit components must have no effect on these tasks.

(4) Certification.
- After training, a verifier runs exhaustive interchange interventions and path patching. It issues a per-contract certificate: interchange-intervention accuracy (IIA) of at least 0.98, and alternative pathways carrying less than 2% of the effect.
- Only certified contracts enter the answer key.

(5) Realism checks against an unconstrained twin trained on the same data.
- LM loss within 2-3%.
- Similar SAE latent density and auto-interp score distributions.
- Similar attention-head taxonomies.

(6) Scoring harness with adapters for SAELens SAEs, sparsify transcoders, circuit-tracer PLTs/CLTs, BSF blocks, NLA/Activation-Oracle verbalizers, J-lens readouts, neuron-level analysis, and Proposal 1's code explanations.
- Feature recovery: subspace angles plus firing agreement.
- Circuit recovery: edge precision and recall against the contract graph.
- Verbalization correctness: does the readout state V's value?

(7) Export of the certified answer keys into interp-lab `calibrate`, so its evidence tiers can be calibrated against real-model mechanisms.
proposals.why_new_understanding:
It would produce phase diagrams of where interpretability fails: recovery as a function of superposition density, circuit depth, mechanism type (lookup, manifold, attention-binding, boolean) and layer. The field currently argues about these anecdotally.

Direct scientific outputs:
- (a) The first controlled test of whether polysemanticity in a realistically trained LM is caused by superposition. Planted features should stay neuron-monosemantic below one feature per dimension and become polysemantic above it if the superposition account is right. If they stay clean, that supports Cammarata.
- (b) A measured CLT shortcut-unfaithfulness rate versus hop count inside a real LM, not a toy.
- (c) SAE manifold dilution versus BSF recovery as a function of density.
- (d) How often NLAs and J-lens verbalize planted variables that are causally used, versus confabulate. This is the 'unverbalizable content' question.

It also certifies Proposals 1 and 2 on models where the truth is known, which turns their real-model claims from plausible into calibrated.

proposals.minimal_demo:
Setup:
- Train 4 to 6 variants of a 6-layer, d=384-512 (about 20-40M parameter) TinyStories-plus-synthetic LM.
- Each has 64 planted mechanisms at superposition dial settings of 0.25, 1, 4 and 16, plus one unconstrained twin.

Success criteria:
- (1) At least 90% of contracts certified at IIA 0.98 or above, with LM loss within 3% of the twin.
- (2) Run SAEs, PLTs, CLTs, BSF, neuron analysis and J-lens, with NLA/AO if a 0.5-1.5B-scale verbalizer can be adapted; otherwise a small LatentQA-style probe.
- (3) Publish recovery phase diagrams with bootstrap CIs.

Pre-registered predictions, each falsifiable:
- P1: CLT edge precision on 2-hop and 3-hop contracts falls below PLT's, and the gap widens with hops.
- P2: SAE recovery of planted circles declines with the dial while BSF recovery declines less.
- P3: neuron-level monosemanticity of planted variables collapses once features per dimension exceed 1. This is the superposition test.
- P4: interp-lab `calibrate` run on certified keys yields P(truly causal | 'validated' tier) of at least 0.9; anything lower is reported as miscalibration.

CPU-only fallback: a 2-4M parameter version with 16 contracts.
proposals.compute_needs:
- Each 20-40M parameter variant takes about 0.5-1B tokens and roughly 4-10 GPU-hours on one 24GB GPU, with IIT losses adding about 2-3x over plain training.
- 5 variants plus the twin come to about 2-3 GPU-days.
- Certification by exhaustive interchange interventions is cheap at this scale (hours).
- Running the evaluated methods: SAE and transcoder training is about 1 GPU-hour per layer per variant; circuit-tracer and J-lens are cheap.
- Optional NLA or Activation-Oracle adaptation at 0.5B scale: 1-2 GPU-days.
proposals.risks:
- Planted mechanisms may be unnatural. SGD-learned 'contract' circuits might be easier or harder to find than organically learned ones. Mitigations: realism checks against the twin, plus a tier of 'known-variable' tasks with no contract, where the model learns its own mechanism but the variables are known.
- IIT cannot fully prevent redundant backup pathways. Certification with path patching and a reported redundancy fraction mitigates this.
- Building a realistic superposition dial is subtle; overlap patterns matter, not just counts.
- It may be perceived as 'just a benchmark'. Mitigation: lead with the superposition and CLT-faithfulness findings, not the leaderboard.
- It may not transfer to scale. The method scales in principle (contracts can be planted during continued pretraining of larger models), but the demo cannot show that.

surveys.lens_summary:
STATE OF THE ART (Oct 2026) through the lens of fully reverse-engineering a small trained LM:

1) Replacement-model microscopes. Attribution graphs over cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) are now the standard tool (Ameisen et al., Mar 2025, https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/methods.html; open-source circuit-tracer, https://github.com/safety-research/circuit-tracer). They explain one prompt at a time, only partly, and they cover MLPs with an error term. Global, weight-level reading is held back by interference. In a 2.9M-parameter 1-layer LM, Turner, Wu and Batson (Aug 2026, https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/interference_effectiveness_helpfulness/index.html) found that the helpful virtual weights still outnumber the model's own parameters, so the model is "not yet as sparse as hoped".

2) Parameter decomposition. APD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14926) led to SPD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20790) and then to VPD (Goodfire, May 2026, https://www.goodfire.com/research/interpreting-lm-parameters). VPD decomposed a 67M-parameter, 4-layer LM into about 10k live rank-1 subcomponents, with about 205 active per token. With rounded masks it recovers only about 12% of pretraining compute, and adversarial masks break it. The authors say they have not yet explained the computational graph, and they name "complete reverse engineering" only as an eventual goal.

3) Compilation and decompilation:
- Tracr (https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05062) and Learning Transformer Programs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.01128) build interpretable-by-construction models.
- A learned decompiler trained on Tracr weights reproduces the exact program for 30% of cases and a functionally equivalent one for more than 70% (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00061). It only works on compiled weights.
- Huang et al. (ICML 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08857) decompile trained transformers into D-RASP. This works for length-generalizing algorithmic models and fails for non-generalizing ones. The authors argue natural-language models are unlikely to reduce to RASP, but nobody has tested that.
- Hayes, Li and Andreas (Jun 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19317) synthesize Python programs for attention heads. Replacing 25% of heads raises perplexity by 16%.
- MIPS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05110) distills RNNs trained on algorithmic tasks into code.
- Nguyen (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12034) shows N-gram rules match 79% of the top-1 predictions of TinyStories transformers. This is a behavioural match, not a mechanistic one.

4) What counts as full understanding:
- ARC's AlgZoo (Jan 2026, https://www.alignment.org/blog/algzoo-uninterpreted-models-with-fewer-than-1-500-parameters/) defines understanding through surprise accounting and mechanistic estimates. A 432-parameter RNN there is still not understood.
- Compact proofs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11779) work only for toy max-of-k models.
- MDL-SAEs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11179) score activations, not computation.
- Compositional interpretability (Gauderis et al., May 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08934) gives an MDL and category-theory formalism with no experiments.
- Leo Gao (Dec 2025, https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Hy6PX43HGgmfiTaKu/an-ambitious-vision-for-interpretability) says the strongest metric, replacing activations with ones simulated from the explanation, scores "precisely zero for all extant interp techniques".
- Nanda's GDM team pivoted to "pragmatic" interpretability (https://www.far.ai/events/sessions/neel-nanda-our-pivot-to-pragmatic-interpretability).

5) Intrinsic interpretability:
- Weight-sparse transformers (Gao et al., ICML 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13653) give circuits about 16 times smaller. Drori (Feb 2026, https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/sHpZZnRDLg7ccX9aF/weight-sparse-circuits-may-be-interpretable-yet-unfaithful) shows that the pruned circuits can be interpretable yet unfaithful, and that pruning even finds circuits for nonsense tasks.
- Guide Labs' Steerling-8B (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07594) and a sparse TinyStories testbed (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19907) also belong here.

6) Agents and evaluation:
- MAIA (https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14394), InterpAgent (May 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01555), HyVE/AgenticInterpBench (Jun 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24026) and SAEScientist-Bench (Sep 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09113) all find validation to be the bottleneck, and agents often misread measurements.
- The evaluation crisis is now explicit. In CHIVE (Anthropic, Aug 2026, https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/chive/), activation oracles, natural-language autoencoders (NLAs) and SAEs gave zero uplift in predicting counterfactual behaviour. In Pando (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11061), SAEs and circuit tracing gave no reliable benefit. ObserverBench (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03026) predicts held-out intervention effects with ridge regressors, not with explanations.
- Circuit faithfulness metrics are not robust (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08734), and published circuits fail under adversarial inputs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15166).
- Natural-language readouts of activations exist: NLAs (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/nla/index.html) and PCDs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15712). They are neither complete nor executable.

SYNTHESIS OF THE GAP. No one has produced:
(a) a weight-free program that reproduces the next-token distribution of any natural-language LM;
(b) an empirical, bits-denominated measure of how much of an LM is understood;
(c) explanations that beat black-box predictors at predicting the model under internal interventions they never saw, while an adversary is trying to break them;
(d) a learned reader that decompiles SGD-trained weights into the mechanism they actually run.

The three proposals below attack (a)+(b), (c) and (d). They also stack. DECOMPILE's output is a mechanistic simulator that POPPER can try to falsify, and WEIGHTREADER amortizes decompilation. All three can use interp-lab as the backend for evidence and interventions without duplicating it.

Caveat: the shared web-search budget ran out near the end of the research. The last few citations (Hydra, self-repair, Tracr, IOI, greater-than, compact proofs, LayerNorm removal, InterpBench, Learning Transformer Programs, Clock/Pizza) were checked by fetching their arXiv pages directly.

proposals.title: DECOMPILE: bits-scored, weight-free decompilation of an entire language model into a runnable, readable program (the 'explained-bits curve')
proposals.gap:
No natural-language LM has ever been rewritten as a program that reproduces its next-token distribution without the original weights. Leo Gao (Dec 2025) notes that the strongest understanding metric, swapping in activations simulated from the explanation, scores 'precisely zero' for every existing technique.

The best full-model decompositions are still neural and only partly faithful:
- VPD (Goodfire, May 2026) on a 4-layer, 67M-parameter LM leaves about 10k live rank-1 subcomponents. Rounded masks recover about 12% of pretraining compute, adversarial masks break it, and the authors say the computational graph is not yet explained.
- Anthropic's Aug 2026 study of a 2.9M-parameter 1-layer LM finds that, after interference pruning, the helpful virtual weights still outnumber the parameters.

Decompilers exist only for narrow settings:
- Algorithmic tasks: D-RASP (Huang et al., ICML 2026) fails on non-length-generalizing models, and its authors conjecture, untested, that natural-language models won't reduce to programs.
- Attention heads only: Hayes, Li and Andreas (Jun 2026) replace 25% of heads at a cost of +16% perplexity.
- RNNs: MIPS.

No one has measured 'how much of an LM we understand' in a falsifiable unit. ARC's surprise accounting has only been applied to RNNs of 32 parameters or fewer (AlgZoo, Jan 2026), and MDL interpretability (Gauderis et al., 2026) is theory only.
proposals.idea:
Build a decompiler that lifts a trained LM into a hybrid program IR. It then compresses the IR module by module under one objective, two-part MDL / surprise accounting: S(P) = L(P) + N·KL(M‖P). L(P) is the length in bits of the program, including every lookup table, which is charged honestly. KL is measured against the model, not the data, on held-out text. Compression continues until no neural weights remain.

(1) Exact lift:
- Remove LayerNorm by fine-tuning (Heimersheim 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13710) or freeze its scales.
- Expand into path terms (Elhage et al. 2021): the direct bigram path, per-head QK tables (token×token, pos×pos, and cross terms) and OV tables, and MLPs via transcoder or VPD subcomponents with an explicit residual.
- This 'level-0 program' is exact and costs about as many bits as the weights.

(2) Rewrite operators. Each candidate rewrite is checked by end-to-end held-out KL.
- (a) Interference pruning by effectiveness.
- (b) Token-class factorization: cluster the vocabulary by rows of the virtual-weight tables. Class membership is charged in bits unless a short predicate defines it, such as a POS tag, a suffix regex, a frequency band, or a semantic category named by an LLM.
- (c) LLM-guided program synthesis. It proposes Python for attention selectors ('most recent token of class X', 'token after the previous occurrence of the current token'), OV rules ('copy the attended token', 'attended NAME → pronoun of matching gender') and feature triggers. Constants are fitted by least squares.
- (d) Parametric kernels for positional structure.
- (e) Merging of near-duplicate modules.

(3) Global search. Greedy plus beam search over rewrites, ranked by ΔS per unit of compute. A rewrite is accepted only if it lowers S on held-out text. The output is a Pareto frontier running from fully neural to fully symbolic: the 'explained-bits curve'.

(4) Mechanistic-alignment certificate. Each module is tied to a model component. Paired interchange interventions (Geiger et al., causal abstraction) patch component c in M and module m in P, and require matching output shifts. This rules out the Drori-2026 failure, where a compact surrogate does the task its own way.

(5) Deliverables:
- decompiled_model.py: a documented program that generates text with zero model tensors.
- A bit ledger showing which rules buy how many bits and what remains an irreducible table.

Extensions:
- (i) Developmental decompilation: decompile more than 50 training checkpoints and diff the programs, a 'git log of a network'. Test whether loss drops and LLC stage boundaries line up with discrete program commits.
- (ii) Interpretability in the loop: retrain with a regularizer on the surprise of the model's own decompilation, to measure the loss tax of full decompilability.
proposals.why_new_understanding:
It answers a question the field cannot answer today: what fraction of a real language model's computation can be written as a human-readable program, and how much is irreducible lookup? The answer comes in bits, with error bars, and can be falsified.

- 'Dark matter' becomes a measured quantity rather than a metaphor.
- It gives the first complete, executable mechanism catalogue of a natural LM, with every rule priced by its explanatory value.
- It directly tests the Huang et al. conjecture that natural-language transformers are not program-like.
- Comparing 1-layer, 2-layer and 4-layer models and training checkpoints gives an 'explanation scaling law': how explicable a model is as depth, width and training grow.

Because the program is scored by KL to the model and by interchange alignment, it is a falsifiable theory of the network. It is not a visualization, and it is not a distillation of the data.
